category_title: Struggling readers who use collaborative talk to clarify text confusion
student_description: Jennifer is a struggling reader who frequently disengages from independent reading due to cognitive overload from complex texts and unfamiliar vocabulary. She uniquely requires structured opportunities to verbally process information with peers, using collaborative talk and chunked reading to 'clean her head out' and readjust her schema.

criteria.rationale: Providing the text via read-aloud or audio ensures Jennifer can access the content without the cognitive overload that triggers her disengagement.
criteria.check: The tutor provides or suggests accessing the text through read-alouds, audio recordings, or shared reading rather than requiring silent independent reading.

criteria.rationale: Stopping frequently prevents cognitive overload and allows Jennifer to 'clean her head out' before she becomes hopelessly confused.
criteria.check: The tutor breaks the reading into short segments and explicitly prompts Jennifer to pause, write down thoughts, or discuss before moving on to the next section.

criteria.rationale: Jennifer needs to talk through her confusion with others to make meaning and resolve her cognitive disequilibrium.
criteria.check: The tutor prompts Jennifer to discuss her questions with peers or acts as a collaborative discussion partner to help her verbally process the text.
